sentences.text: THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This is claimant's appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 05.09.2013.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 05.09.2013 at about 11-30 a.m. he along with one Dundappa Kamatgi was proceeding on the left side of N.H.50 main road, near Muttagi cross of B-Bagewadi.

At that time, a cruiser jeep bearing registration No.GJ-12/X-9959 (hereinafter referred as "the offending vehicle"), came in a high speed, in rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
He sustained multiple injuries.
Despite, prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
He has suffered partial permanent disability affecting his earning capacity.
He was earning Rs.8,000/- p.m.
As owner and insurer, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.

5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
Respondent No.2 has also disputed that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1.
Two witnesses as P.W.2 and P.W.3 including the doctor.

He has relied upon Exs.P.1 to 14.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as R.W.1 and Exs.R.1 and 2 got marked.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.1,74,100/- with interest at 9% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:
For Pain and Suffering Rs.39,000/-

For loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/-

10. Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

11. During the course of arguments, the learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that while P.W.3 has assessed the disability at 30- 35% of the whole body, the Tribunal has erred in taking the whole body disability at 10%.
Loss of future prospects is not awarded.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

13. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
14.
As evident from the impugned judgment and award, P.W.3, Dr.Nagathan, senior orthopedic surgeon, District Hospital, Vijayapura has examined the petitioner for the purpose of determining disability.
He is no the treating doctor.
He has issued disability certificate to the effect that the petitioner has suffered 30-35% disability of the left lower limb.
Consequently, the Tribunal is justified in taking the whole body disability at 10%.
Since the accident is of the year 2013, the notional income taken by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- p.m. is correct.
Though the Tribunal has accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent partial disability, it has not granted any compensation towards loss of income due to disability.

While calculating loss of earning capacity,
loss of future prospects is required to be added.
Since the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 35 years, the appropriate multiplier is 16 and 40% of the income is required to be added for calculating loss of future prospects.
Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.9,800/-.

With these components, the loss of future earnings is Rs.9,800/-
x 12 x 16 x 10/100= Rs.1,88,160/-.
15.

Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered, period of treatment, medical bills produced,
the compensation granted under the remaining heads are just and reasonable and they require no enhancement.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,62,274/- as against Rs.1,74,114/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation.
(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order with interest.
(Minus the compensation already paid/deposited)
(iv) Vide order dated 20.01.2023, the petitioner is not entitled to interest for delay of 124 days on the enhanced compensation.
(v) Send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
